Linde plc operates as an industrial gas company in the United States, China, Germany, the United Kingdom, Australia, Mexico, Brazil, and internationally. It offers atmospheric gases, including oxygen, nitrogen, argon, and rare gases; and process gases, such as hydrogen, helium, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, electronic gases, specialty gases, acetylene, etc. The company also designs and constructs turnkey process plants for third-party customers, as well as for the gas businesses in various locations consist of air separation, hydrogen, synthesis, olefin, and natural gas plants. It serves a range of industries comprising healthcare, chemicals and energy, manufacturing, metals and mining, food and beverage, and electronics. Linde plc was founded in 1879 and is based in Woking, the United Kingdom.

U.S. stocks are trading near record highs. But despite the strong performance, they are being beat by global stocks. A leading industrialized global stock market index, the ETF EAFE (EFA), has surged 22% year to date, while the leading emerging market ETF (EEM) has gained 26%. The S&P 500 is no slacker, but is up "only" 12% year to date, well below the international indices. With continued worries over the state of the U.S. economy, and some talk of stagflation, global stocks (especially those that pay dividends) are a potential option for investors. Lagging U.S. markets are not the norm. Indeed, over the past five years, the S&P 500 has advanced 100% compared to a 46% gain in EAFE and a 23% gain in the EEM. But underperformance has given global stocks a valuation advantage, particularly in the area of dividends. Consider that the EAFE dividend yield of 2.82% is roughly 175 basis points higher than the comparable S&P 500 dividend yield. In our view, investing in international income stocks is one way to increase portfolio diversification while reducing sensitivity to volatile U.S. interest rates. Turning to risks associated with investing in international stocks, we note the impact of currency exchange and geopolitical turmoil.
